newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK, China to crackdown on illegal young migrants.
newsitem.headline: HK, China to crackdown on illegal young migrants.

text.p: Police in Hong Kong and China's southern Guangdong province have agreed on new measures to crack down on mainland Chinese children sneaking into the territory, local television reported on Tuesday.
Eddie Hui, commissioner of police in Hong Kong, was quoted by ATV station as saying that the territory would be setting up a special taskforce and would be stepping up cooperation with China.
"We will liaise closely with our Chinese counterparts across the border. We will exchange information and intelligence," he told reporters.
Guangdong police will also tackle the problem by increasing border patrols, Hui said.
The agreement coincides with a sharp rise in the number of mainland Chinese children caught sneaking into Hong Kong, in most cases to join one or both parents in the territory.
Some 1,500 mainland children have been caught moving into Hong Kong so far in 1997, twice that for the whole of 1996, the station reported, quoting police figures.
The influx surged after rumours began spreading in southern China that amnesty would be given to illegal migrant children.
But the Hong Kong government has repeatedly stressed that everybody, including children, would be sent back.
The problem of illegal Chinese immigrants is a major headache for the territory, which reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.
Regulations controlling access to Hong Kong are likely to remain in force for the foreseeable future.
